methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: AI Ready Roanoke evaluates use for new technology in Roanoke Valley - Roanoke Times
signals.signal_reading: The 'AI Ready Roanoke' initiative suggests intentional capability-building in a secondary city, but without details on depth of technical training versus surface-level adoption, it risks remaining an aspiration rather than redistributing the concentrated expertise currently centered in NoVA.

signals.title: Amazon bows to local backlash over AI data centers, scraps plans to build four new facilities in Northern Virginia — site to be repurposed for mixed-use and residential development. - Tom's Hardware
signals.signal_reading: Local backlash forcing Amazon to scrap four NoVA data centers signals infrastructure saturation and community resistance in the core hub, potentially slowing the very concentration that drives Virginia's AI economy without activating alternative regional centers.

signals.title: Military spouse uses AI to help veterans navigate VA benefits - DC Military
signals.signal_reading: A military spouse independently building AI tools to navigate VA benefits demonstrates grassroots, mission-driven AI capability emerging outside traditional tech hubs, suggesting distributed problem-solving capacity could develop through peer networks in defense-adjacent communities.

signals.title: Virginia governor orders statewide plan to address AI cyberattacks - StateScoop
signals.signal_reading: A governor's executive order for statewide AI cybersecurity planning implies platform-level, top-down AI adoption across government rather than deep technical fluency, pointing toward shallow but broadly distributed implementation through vendor solutions.

signals.title: Roanoke County celebrates new Career and Technology Center opening - WFIR News
signals.signal_reading: Roanoke County's new Career and Technology Center opening creates physical infrastructure for hands-on technical skill development outside metro areas, providing the necessary foundation for distributed deep capability if curriculum evolves beyond traditional trades to include AI/data fluency.
